params.introduction: This is the unbound authoring template for one or more authenticated SISU model rows. Every analysis is row-local: a one-row report displays that row directly, while a multi-row report composes independently authenticated row-local FigureSpecs into labeled subplot blocks before report execution. Row layout is presentation only; it does not impose discrete-versus-continuous scientific authorities, and every current report row may be a continuously sampled model. The conditioning variable s uses one continuous color scale within each figure, so the same value has the same color. Replicas remain separately trained copies rather than pooled observations. Timing comes from typed task metadata: nominal figures have no perturbation marker, bounded perturbations show their authenticated interval, and reach-focused hold-task analyses select the movement epoch without inventing one for catch trials. Every included FigureManifest and optional scalar projection is an exact authenticated parent. Missing, duplicated, incompatible, or scientifically inapplicable evidence fails closed instead of being copied from another row or filled in.

figures.caption: Training adaptive diagnostics. Per-knot lambda and damage-ratio trajectories are plotted against global training batch, with conditioning s read from the continuous colorbar and target-ratio traces distinguished by line style. The training adversary's authored temporal support is a property of the retained training row and must not be read as a movement-epoch mask or as the later analysis-time reach perturbation bank.

sections.framing: The adaptive traces show how each model row adjusted its per-knot adversary weights and tracked the authored damage-ratio targets during training. They describe the training-time adversary, not the separate analysis-time perturbation bank.
sections.title: Training diagnostics

figures.caption: Trial-averaged hand paths by conditioning level after rotating every target direction into the common reach-aligned frame. Equal data scaling preserves path curvature, the colorbar identifies s, and no perturbation marker applies.

Forward velocity through task-relative time for the authenticated trained row, separated into training-support and held-out-support panels. Bands retain the analysis aggregation. Task-compatible comparator profiles are neutral reference traces and appear only when their own exact authorities match the row's typed task contract; they are not additional model rows. These are nominal reaches.

Motor command projected onto the reach direction through task-relative time. Positive values drive toward the target and negative values oppose the reach; conditioning s is read from the shared color scale and no perturbation marker applies.
Peak forward velocity versus conditioning for training-support and held-out reaches.

sections.framing: The reach-aligned trajectory, velocity-profile, and command-profile figures ask how ordinary reaching changes with conditioning. Target directions are expressed in a common reach-aligned frame where forward points toward the target and lateral points across it; when two model rows are requested, report composition stacks the same row-local panels rather than changing the analyses.
sections.title: Nominal reach behaviour

figures.caption: Peak lateral deviation, signed response through time, recovery time, and reach-aligned perturbed paths for the authenticated analysis-time pulse bank. Timing markers come from the retained perturbation schedule, path panels use equal spatial scale, opposite pulse signs remain separate, and conditioning s uses one continuous colorbar. For a hold task, the pulse onset is anchored to the typed movement epoch rather than to whole-trial time.

sections.framing: The matched lateral-pulse figure asks how a task-relative lateral pulse moves the hand off course and how the controller recovers. The analysis is performed independently for every model row; multiple rows are presentation subplots only.
sections.title: Matched disturbance rejection

figures.caption: Norms of selected local controller blocks versus conditioning s at retained reach landmarks. K_y maps a small observed plant-state change to a command change and W maps hidden state to emitted command. Larger norms mean stronger local sensitivity, not automatically better control.

Local conditioning derivatives and changes from the s=0 reference for the feedback gain K_y. The two quantities answer different questions and retain independent axes; descriptive variation does not by itself establish a controller mechanism.

Fractions of the plant-state input map B_y and conditioning input map B_s that point into hidden-state directions the readout can immediately express. B_y and B_s are categories, not conditioning values, and replica traces remain separate.

sections.framing: The controller input-output figures summarize local controller sensitivities along the authenticated nominal reach. Each model row keeps its replicas separate, so controller differences are not mixed with differences between retained trial partitions.
sections.title: Controller input-output view

figures.caption: Intrinsic hidden-map spectral radius at accepted hold-at-goal constrained roots versus conditioning s, with root and replica identities preserved. Root coverage and zero-root cells remain part of the authenticated analysis rather than being inferred from the plot.

Intrinsic hidden-map spectral radius through task-relative time along a nominal reach. This is not closed-loop stability; the full plant-plus-controller finite-horizon induced gain is reported separately by the induced-gain projection.

Trial-averaged hidden-state trajectories for one authenticated model row projected onto that row's own leading principal-component subspaces. Reach direction uses line style, conditioning uses the continuous colorbar, and equal aspect preserves geometry. The fitted basis is local to the row and cannot align coordinates across rows.

sections.framing: The controller state figures describe intrinsic hidden-state structure and nominal hidden trajectories. These are controller-local quantities rather than the full plant-controller loop. Hidden coordinates are model-specific; basis-invariant spectra and within-model geometry may be read directly, while raw directions must not be compared across model rows.
sections.title: Controller state view

figures.caption: Spectral geometry of accepted coupled plant-controller equilibria for the authenticated model row. A spectral radius below one is locally contracting and a value above one has at least one expanding linearized mode; accepted-root counts describe searched coverage only.

sections.framing: The coupled-equilibrium geometry evaluates the full plant-plus-controller linearization only at solver roots that pass the complete task-equilibrium gate. Coverage is finite-bank local evidence, not a claim about nonlinear or global stability.
sections.title: Coupled full-loop roots

figures.caption: Finite-horizon induced gain gamma across conditioning for the authenticated model row, with retained replicate variation. The result is limited to the authored target, horizon, disturbance channel, and running cost; any damage-curvature transform shown by the analysis is not full value-function curvature.

sections.framing: The induced-gain projection follows the full linear time-varying plant-plus-controller loop along the retained nominal reach and reports finite-horizon induced gain gamma. Lower gain means less worst-case amplification under the authored disturbance and running-cost contract.
sections.title: Threat-coupled robustness

figures.caption: Replica-resolved eigenvalues of the intrinsic hidden-state Jacobian at accepted constrained roots. Equal data scaling and the unit circle separate locally contracting from expanding modes; these are not full plant-controller stability results.

sections.framing: The appendix exposes the intrinsic hidden-map eigenvalues underlying the radius summary while preserving their local, controller-only interpretation.
sections.title: Hidden eigenspectrum appendix

sections.not_applicable_reason: The current report graph has no row-local scalar-projection products. Historical continuous-cohort table products are not copied into a different model row or a composed multi-row report.
sections.title: Scalar summaries
